## Sep 20 Performance: The Data Speaks Volumes

Let's break down yesterday's numbers. 11 wins, 4 losses, 73.3% accuracy rate. That's not luck—that's statistical modeling at work. When you're hitting nearly three out of every four picks, you're operating well above league baseline.

## Breaking Down the Winners

Our 60%+ confidence picks went 7-2. That's a 77.8% conversion rate on high-probability outcomes. The Pirates (62%), Cubs (61%), Guardians (61%), and Mariners (61%) all delivered exactly as the model projected. Even our coin-flip picks at 50% split evenly—Tigers/Sox went our way, Braves/Astros didn't. That's variance working exactly as expected.

## Where We Missed

Two losses in the 60% confidence tier: Rangers and Astros. The Rangers pick had solid underlying metrics, but baseball operates on a 162-game sample for a reason. Individual game variance exists. That 60% win probability means we expect to lose 4 out of every 10. Yesterday we lost 2 out of 9 in that range. Still ahead of projection.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick: Blue Jays Over Orioles

Look at the Sep 21 slate. The model's running the numbers and one matchup stands out: Blue Jays at Orioles. Toronto gets the edge at 54% win probability. This is a pitcher's duel—Trey Yesavage taking the mound for the Jays against Shane Baz for Baltimore.

## The Yesavage-Baz Matchup By The Numbers

54% isn't a screaming edge, but edges are edges. Trey Yesavage brings the data advantage here. When you're looking at starting pitcher metrics, park factors, bullpen availability, and recent offensive trends, Toronto grades out slightly ahead. Shane Baz has shown vulnerability in recent outings, and the Jays' lineup has the statistical profile to exploit it.

This isn't a slam dunk—those don't exist in September baseball. But 54% probability means over a large sample, this exact scenario wins more than it loses. That's all we're looking for.
